subject: Crestline renewal: retainer + usage hedge with granular burst tiers
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@crestline.media>
To: Olga Petrova <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Das <samir.das@crestline.media>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — commit + surge tiers

Hi Olga,

Hope you're well. We're kicking off our renewal planning for Sept and want to lock a plan that lets us scale from 6M to ~9M tokens/month over the next 12 months without a sticker shock. Key asks from procurement and engineering: 
- A predictable price-hold window (6–9 months) during the busiest Q4 ramp.
- A hedge/retainer structure that reduces unit price at steady commit points but lets us burst at defined tiers.
- Service credits tied to p99 latency and cold-starts for the dedicated endpoints.

Can you share example structures (discounts, credits, true-up mechanics) that Redwood has used for customers moving from mid-commit to a larger retainer? We're also attaching the internal forecast.

Timeline: procurement needs a term sheet and high-level pricing by end of this week to route to legal.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Li
Head of ML Platforms, Crestline Media
From: Olga Petrova <olga@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@crestline.media>, Samir Das <samir.das@crestline.media>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — commit + surge tiers

Emma — thanks for the clear asks and forecast. Attached is a short note and a draft term sheet with three options so you can see the tradeoffs quickly. High-level: 

Option A — 12m fixed retainer (best unit price)
- 12-month committed spend (covers projected 9M tokens/month)
- 18% off list unit price, quarterly true-ups, standard overage at list
- 90-day price-hold on CPU/GPU-enabled variants after signature

Option B — Staged uplift + hedged burst tiers (recommended for ramp)
- 6m initial retainer for first 3 months, staged add at month 4 and month 8 to reach 9m
- Upfront credit pool: $60k applied to overage in first quarter (one-time)
- Burst tiers: defined buckets (0–9m, 9–12m, 12m+) with capped marginal overage rates and a quarterly consumption true-up
- Performance SLA: SLA credit of up to 5% invoice if p99 latency > SLA for two consecutive weeks

Option C — Short price-hold + consumption overlay
- 6-month price-hold vs current rates, then reprice to tiered committed bands
- Lower initial credit but more conservative escalation for discounts

Operational notes: we can bake an explicit burst waiver for Q4 for new customers on Option B (limited to first 90 days) and include an engineering runbook for prefix/KV caching to reduce token usage.

I've CC'd Ben and Marissa — they'll review the concession budget. I attached the term sheet (Crestline_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf) and an SLA benchmark file. Can you confirm procurement's must-have items so we can tighten numbers?

Best,
Olga Petrova
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: Crestline_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (application/pdf), SLA_Benchmarks_2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrova <olga@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — concession framing

Team — quick internal take after skimming the draft:
- Option B is the right commercial shape for a ramping media customer. It balances upside and protects price.
- We should tighten the upfront credit (propose $40k vs $60k) and convert remaining concession into a performance-locked credit (only payable if SLAs not met).
- Avoid an open-ended burst waiver — offer a 90-day Q4 waiver capped at 20% above committed tokens; excess billed at a premium.
- If Crestline signs a 12m upfront retainer (Option A), we can stretch to 20% discount but need VP approval for anything > 18%.

Marissa — can you confirm if we have latitude on the SLA credit structure? Vivek, if we need to go above 18% to close an upsell, I recommend we package that as a multi-year concession tied to a 24m commit.

Ben
From: Olga Petrova <olga@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@crestline.media>, Samir Das <samir.das@crestline.media>, Procurement Team <procurement@crestline.media>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — retainer + usage hedge (revised)

Emma / Samir — per internal alignment we've updated the draft with the following changes (attached):
- Upfront credit reduced to $40k and restructured as a bill credit applied to Q3 overages only.
- SLA credit now performance-locked: up to 5% of invoice if p99 latency > SLA for two consecutive weeks; credits capped at $25k per quarter.
- Burst waiver: Q4 90-day waiver with a 20% cap above committed monthly tokens, after which overage = 1.5x standard overage rate.
- Added a 'reconciliation true-up' every quarter to keep billing simple and predictable.

Next steps suggested for procurement: 
1) Confirm the preferred option (A, B, or C) and any absolute non-starters (e.g., open burst waivers).
2) If Option B is chosen, confirm timing of staged uplifts (month 4 and 8 proposed).
3) Legal review — we can issue a DocuSign-ready term sheet once procurement confirms wording.

I've uploaded the updated term sheet and created a DocuSign envelope (link below). If procurement can commit to the staged uplift timing, we can lock a 6-month price-hold for the first stage.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/crestdoc/47f2a
Term sheet attached: Crestline_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf

Regards,
Olga
From: Procurement Team <procurement@crestline.media>
To: Olga Petrova <olga@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@crestline.media>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — retainer + usage hedge (revised)

Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround. Crestline procurement has reviewed the revised term sheet with finance. We are comfortable with Option B (staged uplift + hedge) subject to two requests: 
1) Add a one-off Q4 burst cap waiver for the ramp that explicitly applies to the first 120 days after the first staged uplift (rather than calendar Q4). This gives us runway if the campaign starts early.
2) Can you confirm invoice cadence? We prefer monthly invoices with the quarterly true-up applied as a credit/charge the following invoice cycle.

If you can accept the above, we can sign the DocuSign this afternoon and kick off legal review on our side.

Best,
Samir Das
Procurement Manager, Crestline Media
